title: Stories of Faith — Reading and Writing with Purpose
description: Test your knowledge of grammar, reading comprehension, writing, and vocabulary!

questions.question: Which word in this sentence is a noun? 'Moses led the people through the desert.'
questions.explanation: Moses is a noun because it names a person. Nouns name people, places, or things.

questions.question: Which word in this sentence is a verb? 'God created the heavens and the earth.'
questions.explanation: Created is a verb because it shows an action — something God did.

questions.question: In Psalm 23, who is the shepherd?
questions.explanation: In Psalm 23, David says 'The Lord is my shepherd,' meaning God is the shepherd who cares for us.

questions.question: What does every complete sentence need?
questions.explanation: Every complete sentence needs a subject (who or what it is about) and a predicate (what the subject does).

questions.question: What punctuation mark goes at the end of a question?
questions.explanation: A question mark (?) goes at the end of an interrogative sentence — a sentence that asks a question.

questions.question: What does the word 'diligent' mean?
questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful. Proverbs 12:24 teaches that diligent hands will rule.

questions.question: What are context clues?
options: Hints in a sentence that help you figure out a word's meaning
questions.explanation: Context clues are words and sentences around an unknown word that give hints about its meaning.

questions.question: When writing a book report about a Bible story, which of these should you include?
options: Only the ending of the story
questions.explanation: A good book report includes the characters, the setting, a summary of what happened (beginning, middle, end), and the lesson of the story.
